Bayesian preservation model

Source: R/tph.R
tpbhm.Rd

A Bayesian linear model of a preservation score (or any outcome) on burial conditions and measurements, with a normal prior on each coefficient and the noise variance fixed at the least-squares residual variance (an empirical Bayes plug-in), so that the posterior is normal in closed form. An informative prior on a treatment (say, that quicklime preserves) is set through pm and psd, and the data revise it. With groups (cemeteries, sites) the mean residual of each group is shrunk towards 0 by the method of moments: tau2 is the variance between the group means beyond what the noise explains.

Usage

tpbhm(y, x, grp = NULL, pm = 0, psd = 10, level = 0.95)

Arguments

y

The outcome: finite numbers, at least two cases. A clpre list from clprep() is taken too (the taph-* presets): its elements fill the arguments by name.

x

The predictors: a numeric matrix or data frame of finite numbers, one row per case (code a factor as indicator columns first).

grp

NULL, or the group of each case: labels, at least two groups.

pm, psd

The prior means and standard deviations of the intercept and the coefficients: one number each or one per term (psd positive).

level

The confidence level of the intervals: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

A list: coef, a data frame with one row per term (term, mean, sd, the interval lo, hi, ppos the posterior probability that the coefficient is above 0, prior the prior's standard deviation); sigma, the noise standard deviation; tau2; groups, NULL or a data frame with one row per group (group, n, raw the mean residual, shrink the factor, pooled the shrunk intercept); fitted; level.

References

Gelman, A., Carlin, J. B., Stern, H. S., Dunson, D. B., Vehtari, A. and Rubin, D. B. (2013). Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed. CRC Press. doi:10.1201/b16018

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(lime = rbinom(30, 1, 0.5), temp = rnorm(30, 12, 3))
y <- 0.3 + 0.2 * d$lime - 0.01 * d$temp + rnorm(30, sd = 0.05)
tpbhm(y, d, grp = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), 10), pm = c(0, 0.2, 0))$coef
#>          term        mean          sd          lo          hi      ppos prior
#> 1 (Intercept) 0.173071063 0.045858883  0.08318930 0.262952821 0.9999197    10
#> 2        lime 0.184805792 0.016328473  0.15280257 0.216809011 1.0000000    10
#> 3        temp 0.001683087 0.003552176 -0.00527905 0.008645224 0.6821854    10
